body:
**Changes:**

- Publish the existing implementation: buffer/crypto write-path improvements, teardown and user-removal handling, WireGuard batching with selective Linux GSO, and native UDP optimizations.
- Include the previously completed original five-workload TCP/UDP evidence and the separately measured SS2022 → WireGuard supplement, preserving their original reports, summaries and independent audits unchanged.
- Compare the measured **before** frozen official `0888beb38a9ba45440557175e71ce21cf8ba3b13` with the measured **after** frozen hybrid `1a52c36f162f75d68abf8d331dfea8c12e9f5640`. These measurements do **not** benchmark current fork `dev` `a9e521b22ee7b3300b2f5e45ca6535d199b767c3`.

**Project impact:**

The completed measurements show workload-dependent goodput changes and reduced observed upload loss in the four Shadowsocks UDP cases, with regressions retained below. They do not establish universal latency/download wins, WAN performance, sustained UDP capacity, or isolated causal GSO/batching effects. This PR targets `dev`; no merge-ready or mergeability claim is made here. The target's existing commits are not merged, rebased or rewritten by this description.

## Previous completed measurements: official → hybrid

All values are **before → after**. Throughput is **decimal MB/s**, not MiB/s (`Mbit/s ÷ 8`); latency is **microseconds (us)**. Display values are the supplied three-decimal `Decimal(str(value))` / `ROUND_HALF_UP` values. Throughput is the median of seven matched per-round directional rates. Established RTT and fresh application-flow setup/first-response are medians of seven per-round medians, not pooled observations. Established latency uses 256 verified 64-byte exchanges per round with 32 warmups excluded; first-response uses eight fresh application flows per round with proxy/WireGuard prewarmed, **not cold WireGuard setup or SOCKS CONNECT**.

Cohort **O** is the original five routes: 40 primary rows / 280 timed cells across four builds and TCP/UDP. Cohort **S** is the later **separate SS2022 → WireGuard supplement**: eight primary rows / 56 timed cells. S was not jointly interleaved with O; showing them together does not pool them into one experiment.

Route/cipher legend: both `ssclassic-*` routes use `chacha20-ietf-poly1305`; both `ss2022-*` routes use `2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm`. VLESS uses encryption `none` over plain TCP with no TLS/XTLS/mux; VMess uses AEAD `chacha20-poly1305` over plain TCP with no TLS/mux. `*-freedom` means direct freedom egress to the verified echo; `*-wireguard` means WireGuard outbound → fixed WireGuard gateway → verified echo.

### TCP

| Route | Cohort | Upload MB/s | Download MB/s | Established RTT us | Setup/first-response us |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ssclassic-freedom | O | 998.406 → 1017.774 | 1055.611 → 1028.154 | 87.271 → 81.352 | 609.915 → 604.059 |
| ss2022-freedom | O | 917.050 → 1000.250 | 796.952 → 872.572 | 91.142 → 84.278 | 657.985 → 662.740 |
| ssclassic-wireguard | O | 121.799 → 172.914 | 169.514 → 181.689 | 274.823 → 292.105 | 1176.969 → 1253.454 |
| ss2022-wireguard | S (separate) | 125.350 → 207.624 | 180.977 → 210.617 | 299.271 → 295.671 | 1269.116 → 1275.048 |
| vless-wireguard | O | 136.272 → 226.003 | 172.523 → 211.557 | 289.965 → 267.054 | 1064.492 → 1080.712 |
| vmess-wireguard | O | 124.419 → 178.011 | 177.952 → 196.965 | 278.904 → 308.914 | 1348.726 → 1287.535 |

TCP uses one application stream, 128 MiB verified payload per direction and an excluded 8 MiB warmup per direction; timing is receiver-ready to final verified byte.

### UDP — controlled burst workload, not sustained capacity

| Route | Cohort | Upload MB/s | Download MB/s | Established RTT us | Setup/first-response us |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ssclassic-freedom | O | 39.859 → 50.535 | 51.340 → 49.438 | 165.321 → 170.177 | 487.985 → 492.325 |
| ss2022-freedom | O | 59.548 → 64.987 | 60.456 → 61.546 | 120.436 → 124.672 | 584.666 → 531.625 |
| ssclassic-wireguard | O | 25.663 → 34.176 | 31.583 → 31.719 | 267.270 → 277.330 | 751.852 → 746.637 |
| ss2022-wireguard | S (separate) | 29.541 → 39.111 | 35.300 → 35.826 | 266.334 → 267.628 | 755.781 → 823.472 |
| vless-wireguard | O | 39.195 → 38.395 | 35.225 → 37.864 | 235.293 → 262.613 | 777.782 → 783.404 |
| vmess-wireguard | O | 36.042 → 40.327 | 35.466 → 39.147 | 299.153 → 269.792 | 1078.748 → 1043.552 |

UDP uses 436 windows of **32 × 1200-byte bursts**, 16742400 offered payload bytes per direction per round, reliable same-route **TCP progress/control barriers**, and a fixed **100-ms receiver-local drain/cutoff**. Unique delivery is verified; DATA is not retransmitted. This is not sustained offered-rate/unpaced UDP capacity and is not TCP-comparable capacity. VLESS/VMess UDP forwarding here runs over raw TCP streams; Shadowsocks uses UDP data transport.

### UDP loss: directional medians and actual aggregate counts

Percentages are medians of seven per-round directional loss percentages. Lost-datagram counts are actual totals across those seven rounds, not counts inferred from the median percentage.

| Route | Cohort | Upload loss % | Download loss % | Upload lost datagrams total | Download lost datagrams total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ssclassic-freedom | O | 19.388 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 19402 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| ss2022-freedom | O | 12.414 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 12390 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| ssclassic-wireguard | O | 17.460 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 18078 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| ss2022-wireguard | S (separate) | 19.703 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 19599 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| vless-wireguard | O | 0.000 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| vmess-wireguard | O | 0.000 → 0.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Hybrid lost **zero observed datagrams in both directions** in these completed UDP cases. This finite controlled-workload observation is not a guarantee of loss-free operation at other offered loads.

### Regressions and interpretation limits

- TCP: ssclassic-freedom download goodput decreased; ssclassic-wireguard and vmess-wireguard established RTT increased; ss2022-freedom, ssclassic-wireguard, separate ss2022-wireguard and vless-wireguard setup/first-response latency increased.
- UDP: ssclassic-freedom download and vless-wireguard upload goodput decreased; established RTT increased for ssclassic-freedom, ss2022-freedom, ssclassic-wireguard, separate ss2022-wireguard and vless-wireguard; setup/first-response latency increased for ssclassic-freedom, separate ss2022-wireguard and vless-wireguard.
- All measurements are on the **same Linux host in fresh private loopback network namespaces, not WAN/internet performance**. Candidate relay CPUs 2,3 are distinct from shared client/gateway/measurement/echo CPUs 0,1; shared support can cap measured goodput. Latency was measured before throughput, without concurrent throughput.
- These are whole-product Git-tree comparisons, not isolated causal GSO/batching effects. `batching-only` is a product snapshot label, not proof that batching is its only difference; the included reports retain all four builds.
- Original TCP running-service snapshots differ by an unexplained `fwupd.service` disappearance. Its cause was not observed; no benchmark-causality inference or all-services-unchanged claim is made. Contemporaneous manual/container Xray PID/command identity was not captured in the original preservation evidence. UDP and supplement snapshots are retained separately.
- No latest sustained/interrupted/failed/recovery measurements are included in these tables, reports or publication scope. No new benchmark is claimed or required for this selected previous-results publication.
